speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
question: What do rites and scripture each accomplish?
premises: Truly (satyam), O Śaṅkara: vow (vrata), giving (dāna), bathing (snāna), austerity (tapas) — dispels (vidāri) becoming's heat (bhavatāpa).
Rites relativized, not despised: heat dispelled by rites.
Contemplation (cintā) of Your (tāvaka) scripture (śāstra) as supreme nectar (parāmṛta), in mind (cetasi), streams (syandati) a bliss-stream (nirvṛtidhārā).
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation.
inference: Two means, two results: rites dispel heat, contemplation streams bliss.
uncertainties: Whether 'vadeśakālam' is obscure or means 'place-and-time under control' is unresolved.
Whether the rites are listed exhaustively or exemplarily is unresolved.
